how_to_combine.position_net: typical_yield × yield_index[s] × price[p] − Σ cost lines − cover cost (if cover) − pump $/acre-inch × irrigation_mm[s] / 25.4 (− overhead lines if included)
how_to_combine.rotation_average: Σ position nets / option.years (equals the mean over positions when every year has exactly one crop or fallow position)
how_to_combine.price: price[p] = typical price × values[p] / median(values); a null value means ERS has no price that year (use the median)
how_to_combine.consistency: With USDA defaults and the comparison's paired price draw this reproduces profit_p50_compare; over all S × P pairs the median differs by sampling only.

notes: Costs are USDA ERS regional averages per planted acre (2021–2025 median), not your farm's costs.
Prices are USDA ERS harvest-period prices 2016–2025 for the Heartland region (nominal dollars), not your local price.
Options are compared on the 30 weather sequences they all share (1991–2020 starts).
reminder: Supports, never replaces, your own budget and your adviser.

insured_losses.method: For each crop and cause: a year is 'hit' when the county's insurance indemnity for that cause was above zero. Loss per acre = that year's indemnity for the cause / all insured acres of the crop in the county that year (nominal dollars; irrigated and dryland practices together). Payouts cover losses beyond the deductible only, so real losses were larger; price declines and area-plan endorsements are not counted.
insured_losses.in_simulation_note: Drought, heat and frost during the season are weather the yield simulation already runs through; add only the causes with in_simulation false to avoid counting twice.
insured_losses.scale: county records (USDA crop insurance), not your field
insured_losses.citation: USDA Risk Management Agency, Cause of Loss Historical Data Files (Summary of Business with month of loss) and State/County/Crop Summary of Business. https://www.rma.usda.gov/tools-reports/summary-of-business/cause-loss

declarations.citation: FEMA, OpenFEMA Dataset: Disaster Declarations Summaries - v2. https://www.fema.gov/openfema-data-page/disaster-declarations-summaries-v2. This product uses the FEMA OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.
declarations.licence: Public (U.S. Government work; OpenFEMA terms of use)

storm_events.citation: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI), Storm Events Database, bulk CSV "details" files. https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/stormevents/
storm_events.note: Reported events; reporting varies by county and decade. Counted: events reported for this county (county events) plus events reported for the NWS forecast zone(s) covering it (zone events: drought, frost/freeze, heat, high wind and winter storms are mostly reported by zone), mapped with the NWS zone-county correlation file (95% of zone reports US-wide could be mapped). A zone's crop damage is split equally between its counties. Crop damage is NCEI's reported estimate in nominal dollars and is often left at zero.
storm_events.in_simulation_note: Drought, heat and frost are weather the yield simulation already runs through; hail, wind, tornado, flood and heavy rain are not simulated.

evidence.definition: weather_seasons = real weather sequences every option runs through (one per start year 1991–2020, each 6 years long, NASA POWER at the field); price_years = USDA ERS harvest-period price years (none outside the US)

n_credit.what: Fertilizer nitrogen you can usually skip on a crop that follows a legume (soybean, pulses, alfalfa, clover): the rules engine's legume credit for that crop (rule 'legume_before_high_n_crop').
n_credit.per_position: n_credit_lb_ac = midpoint of the sourced credit range (lb N/acre, from the crop table's kg N/ha ÷ 1.121); n_credit_range_lb_ac = [low, high]; 0 where no legume credit applies.
n_credit.not_counted: Legume cover crops before corn are flagged by the rules but have no sourced N amount, so they add no credit here. A soil nitrate test is the way to confirm the credit on your field.
n_credit.how_to_value: N saved ($/acre) = n_credit_lb_ac × fertilizer $/lb N (fertilizer_n_price.usd_lb_n or your own).

items.name_es: Cultivo de cobertura para alta biomasa
items.notes: Planting of a multi species mix as a cover crop immediately after harvesting a row crop, but may also be interseeded into a row crop.

items.name_en: Crop rotation: add a different annual crop
items.name_es: Rotación: añadir un cultivo anual distinto
items.notes: Planning of an annual crop rotation with a minimum of two different crop types.

items.name_en: Crop rotation: add a winter or spring annual
items.name_es: Rotación: añadir un cultivo anual de invierno o primavera
items.notes: Addition of a winter annual or small grain to a crop rotation that includes at least two different crop types.

items.name_en: Crop rotation: add a short-term perennial
items.name_es: Rotación: añadir un perenne de corta duración
items.notes: Addition of a short-term perennial (e.g. alfalfa or intermediate wheatgrass) into a crop rotation that currently includes a minimum of two different crops to effectively implement a conservation crop rotation.
Conversion of an irrigated cropping system to a dryland cropping system to improve water use efficiency.

Addition of new crop types to the conservation crop rotation to facilitate building soil organic matter, capturing nitrogen, breaking pest cycles, or other purposes that maintain or enhance natural resources.

costshare.hu_note_en: Higher rate for historically underserved producers (socially disadvantaged, beginning, limited-resource and veteran farmers), where the state publishes one.
costshare.hu_note_es: Tarifa más alta para productores históricamente desatendidos (en desventaja social, principiantes, de recursos limitados y veteranos), si el estado la publica.
costshare.citation: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service, EQIP payment schedule (payment schedule tool).
costshare.caveat_en: Payments need an approved NRCS contract; amounts and eligibility vary. Rates are per acre of the practice as published in the state's EQIP payment schedule, not a promise of payment.
costshare.caveat_es: Los pagos requieren un contrato aprobado con el NRCS; los montos y la elegibilidad varían. Las tarifas son por acre de la práctica según el calendario de pagos EQIP del estado; no son una promesa de pago.
